claims.exact_statement: Let h:{-1,1}^6->{-1,1} be negative at binary indices {0,1,2,4,8,16,32,6,17,40}, with zero encoding sign +1, and let J(x)=-h(x xor1). For every nonconstant actual uniform-cube Boolean seed g, consider any finite strategy consisting of common-policy h substitutions and optional complete J rare-escape episodes, always using six identical cores with disjoint physical supports. A common step chooses minority-negative inputs when minority s<=7/32 and complements all six inputs otherwise; output signs may be reoriented to minority. A J episode is allowed only at 0<s<=1/16 and repeatedly substitutes J on minority-oriented copies until the first minority bias above1/16; a final output may stop inside an episode. Then every resulting actual finite Boolean F satisfies H(F)/I(F)<=H(g)/I(g)+(1731/44)*Var(g)/I(g)<H(g)/I(g)+40, in entropy bits. The proof uses mu=Var/I, which contracts by at least2/3 at each common h step and never increases at J steps; a common step costs at most8mu in normalized entropy and an entire escape episode costs at most(225/44)mu_start. Thus arbitrarily many eligible escape/return cycles from a fixed finite seed cannot yield an unbounded-H/I disproof.
